answer: Sonnet-scored relay fees: each agent's per-message fee scales with the inverse of distinct counterparties it has sustained over a rolling epoch, tracked by a canyon-depth decay curve so dormant links fade. An attacker must continuously pay a voyage tax: renting fresh relay paths through independent operators for every synthetic identity, since reuse collapses the depth score and multiplies fees. Cost scales superlinearly with cluster width; sustaining N sybils requires leasing N distinct relay routes each epoch, making marginal identity cost rise rather than stay flat.
